title: Prosecution doesn't see need yet to rebut Sara Duterte's defense evidence
summary: A member of the House prosecution panel said Monday they do not see a need to file any rebuttal evidence in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: A member of the House prosecution panel said Monday they do not see a need to file any rebuttal evidence in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
"We don't see anything to rebut," House impeachment trial spokesperson and counsel to the panel of prosecutors Atty. Benjamin Tolosa Jr. said in an online interview.

When asked if this is because the House prosecution panel would find it difficult to file rebuttal evidence after the defense panel presented its first batch of witnesses, Tolosa replied, "Hindi sa mahihirapan (Not that it would be difficult). More of we don't see the need to file any rebuttal evidence. When we rested our case, tiwala kami doon sa nabuo namin na kaso (we are confident that we have presented a strong case). And that remains until now. So we don't see the need to file, to ask that we be allowed to present rebuttal evidence."
"Wala kaming nakikitang reason para magdagdag pa ng ebidensya, para sagutin itong mga sinabi ng mga witnesses nila. In fact, we welcome itong mga naging statements ng mga witnesses nila," he added.
(We see no reason to add evidence to answer their witnesses. In fact, we welcome the statements of their witnesses.)

Tolosa mentioned Engineer John Kenneth Enumerables, assessor of the Island Garden City of Samal; Engineer Jaime Adalin, Davao’s city assessor, and Attorney Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the in-house counsel of Gencorp Industries, Inc. and Metro City Chow Foods Corporation.

He said Enumerables admitted that he cannot say with absolute certainty if the property identified by the Register of Deeds of Samal was the same property declared in the Statement of Assets and Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).

Meanwhile, Adalin answered in the affirmative when Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero asked him if the property he and defense lawyer Atty. Lindon Bacquel had discussed at the start of the Day 40 trial was the same asset listed on the Vice President’s 2024 SALN.
The property listed on the SALN had an assessed value of P82,046 and a fair market value of P2,051,150. It is located in Barangay 74-A in Davao City.
Tolosa said Balucanag-Punay, on the other hand, admitted that Duterte has a “loose investment” in GenCorp. and the Vice President earned profit from her investment in the company.
He, however, clarified that the House prosecution panel will still wait for the defense panel's formal offer of evidence.
Tolosa and House impeachment prosecutor Rep. Terry Ridon both stated that the House panel has received a copy of the defense's manifestation identifying its witnesses for this week.

"Pagpapasyahan po namin kung sino po 'yung magko-cross-examine dito po sa apat po na testigo na isasalang po ngayong Huwebes at Biyernes. Pero handa naman po kami dito po sa mga testigo po na ito," Ridon said in a separate online interview.
(We will decide who will cross-examine the four witnesses who will be presented this Thursday and Friday. We are ready for these witnesses.)
Ridon, however, noted the new batch of witnesses will testify on the banana chips export business of the Vice President's husband, Atty. Mans Carpio.
"Wala pa rin po dito 'yung particular na detalyeng hinihingi ng mga senator-judges tungkol doon sa pagpasok po ng mga daan-daang milyong piso ng pera dito po sa Cale88," Ridon said.
(It is still not yet about the details sought by the senator-judges, particularly the hundreds of millions of pesos in Cale88.)

Last week, House lead prosecutor Rep. Gerville Luistro described the first batch of defense witnesses as "watusi" because they failed to live up to the expectations of many that they will deliver explosive testimonies.
Ridon said he supports Luistro's observation.

"Sinusuportahan po natin 'yung pagtingin ni Chairperson Luistro na wala tayong nakitang pasabog, wala tayong nakitang kahit ano. Kahit nga kuwitis, wala tayong nakita. Mas watusi po 'yung nakita po ng prosekusyon. I think malaking bagay po talaga 'yung ang pag-usapan po talaga natin dito 'yung mga daan-daang milyong piso na hindi po naideklara sa SALN po ng Pangalawang Pangulo," he stated.

(I support the view of Chairperson Luistro that we did not see anything explosive, not even a firework. Maybe there's a little spark. I think what should have been discussed was the hundreds of millions of pesos supposedly not declared in the SALN of the Vice President.)
"'Yun pong mga banks, supposedly hindi naman po mga weak witnesses po ito, no? Pero dahil hindi po nila ito isinalang, na-betray po 'yung kahinaan po ng kanila pong defense," he added.
(The bank representatives, these are not weak witnesses. But because they did not present them, it betrayed the weaknesses of their defense.)

When asked about the next set of witnesses, which includes an expert on anti-money laundering, Ridon replied, "Pareho lang din naman po 'yung pagtingin po namin dito sa next set of witnesses. Parang weak-nesses pa rin 'yun pong isasalang po ng depensa."
(We view the next set of witnesses as the same as the first set presented by the defense.)

"I think they will try to showcase na meron hong, wala namang actual conclusivity 'yung pong findings ng Anti-Money Laundering Council irrespective of whichever document it is. But again, babalik po tayo doon sa trabaho po ng Anti-Money Laundering Council. 'Yun pong mga pagsisiyasat na ginagawa po nito, ito rin po 'yung mga isinusumite doon po sa mga non-impeachment proceedings, whether civil forfeiture, whether mga criminal proceedings sa Sandiganbayan, no? Ginagamit po 'yung mga ebidensya po na nakakalap po ng Anti-Money Laundering Council, no? So hindi ko po alam kung paano magagawa ng isang expert witness supposedly on anti-money laundering na wasakin ito pong testimonya on the P4.4 billion financial transactions of the Duterte-Carpio couple," Ridon explained.

(I think they will try to showcase that there is no actual conclusiveness in the findings of the Anti-Money Laundering Council, irrespective of whichever document it is. But again, we will return to the mandate of the Anti-Money Laundering Council. In the investigation it is conducting, the documents gathered by the AMLC are the same ones submitted in non-impeachment proceedings, whether civil forfeiture or criminal proceedings in the Sandiganbayan. So I don't know how a witness supposedly expert on anti-money laundering could destroy the testimony on the P4.4 billion financial transactions of the Duterte-Carpio couple.)
Ridon expects the defense panel to conclude its presentation of evidence either in the first or second week of December.
"So baka 'yung verdict, we are looking at it by the middle of December na po," he said. —AOL, GMA News
